scenario: [LEXP.3.6.1]: `math.degrees(x)` is x times the double nearest 180/math.pi (57.29577951308232), and `math.radians(x)` x times the double nearest math.pi/180 (0.017453292519943295), one correctly rounded multiply each. The expected values are computed in binary64. Facts carry the operand as a `Float` slot `x` or an `Int` slot `n`, so each call is evaluated by the runtime. `degrees pi`: degrees(3.141592653589793) is exactly 180.0. `degrees 11`: degrees(11.0) is 630.2535746439055; the two rounded steps (11.0 * 180.0) / math.pi give 630.2535746439056, one ulp above, so this operand tells the composition from the obvious alternative. `degrees int 11`: the `Int` 11 is converted to `Float` first and gives the same. `radians 180`: radians(180.0) is exactly math.pi. `radians 3`: radians(3.0) is 0.05235987755982989; (3.0 * math.pi) / 180.0 gives 0.05235987755982988. `folded`: the same two operands written as literals, which [LEXP.8.8] has the compiler fold by the same composition. PATH PINNED: FN_DEGREES / FN_RADIANS in libds (`builtins.c`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`), and the constant folder for the literal operands.
rules_ds:
import math

schema A scope logical:
    id: String key
    x: Float mutable
    n: Int mutable

rule degrees_of_pi:
    A a where a.id == "pi" and math.degrees(a.x) == 180.0
->
    log info "degrees pi"

rule degrees_one_rounding:
    A a where a.id == "eleven" and math.degrees(a.x) == 630.2535746439055
->
    log info "degrees 11"

rule degrees_of_an_int:
    A a where a.id == "eleven" and math.degrees(a.n) == 630.2535746439055
->
    log info "degrees int 11"

rule radians_of_180:
    A a where a.id == "deg180" and math.radians(a.x) == math.pi
->
    log info "radians 180"

rule radians_one_rounding:
    A a where a.id == "three" and math.radians(a.x) == 0.05235987755982989
->
    log info "radians 3"

rule folded:
    A a where a.id == "fold" and math.degrees(11.0) == 630.2535746439055 and math.radians(3.0) == 0.05235987755982989
->
    log info "folded"
